Package com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java

Class StronglyConnectedComponents

java.lang.Object
com.phasmidsoftware.gryphon.java.StronglyConnectedComponents
public class StronglyConnectedComponents extends Object
Java façade for strongly-connected-components analysis on directed graphs, using Kosaraju's two-pass algorithm.

A strongly connected component (SCC) is a maximal set of vertices such that there is a directed path from every vertex in the set to every other. Kosaraju's algorithm finds all SCCs in O(V + E) time.

The result is a Map<V, Integer> mapping each vertex to an integer SCC identifier. Vertices that share the same id belong to the same SCC. SCC ids are assigned in topological order of the condensation DAG — the SCC with the smallest id is a "source" component (no incoming cross-edges from other SCCs).

The graph must be directed. Calling these methods on an undirected graph will throw IllegalStateException.

Usage example: 


 Graph<String> g = Graph.directed();
 g.addEdge("A", "B");
 g.addEdge("B", "C");
 g.addEdge("C", "A");   // cycle: A, B, C form one SCC
 g.addEdge("C", "D");   // D is a singleton SCC

 Map<String, Integer> sccs = StronglyConnectedComponents.kosaraju(g);
 sccs.get("A") == sccs.get("B")  // true — same SCC
 sccs.get("A") == sccs.get("D")  // false — different SCCs

 // Count SCCs
 long count = sccs.values().stream().distinct().count();  // 2

 // Group vertices by SCC
 Map<Integer, List<String>> groups = new HashMap<>();
 sccs.forEach((v, id) ->
     groups.computeIfAbsent(id, k -> new ArrayList<>()).add(v));

  • Method Details

    • kosaraju

      public static <V> Map<V,Integer> kosaraju(Graph<V> graph)
      Computes the strongly connected components of a directed graph using Kosaraju's algorithm.

      The graph may have unweighted edges (plain Edge<V>) or weighted edges (WeightedEdge<V, E>) — edge weights are ignored for SCC computation.

      The ids are not fixed. Which vertices share an SCC is a property of the graph and never varies; the integers labelling those components come from traversal order, which is shuffled, so two calls may give the same partition under different ids. Compare partitions rather than ids, or use kosaraju(Graph, java.util.Random).

      Type Parameters:
      V - the vertex type.
      Parameters:
      graph - a directed graph.
      Returns:
      a Map<V, Integer> mapping each vertex to its SCC id; vertices with the same id are in the same SCC.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if graph is undirected.

    • kosaraju

      public static <V> Map<V,Integer> kosaraju(Graph<V> graph, Random random)
      Computes the strongly connected components of a directed graph using Kosaraju's algorithm, drawing its traversal order from random.

      Use this when the component ids themselves must be stable across runs. The partition does not depend on the generator; only the numbering does.

      Pass the generator rather than a seed so that one generator can span several calls, which is what given Random does on the Scala side.

      Type Parameters:
      V - the vertex type.
      Parameters:
      graph - a directed graph.
      random - the generator determining traversal order.
      Returns:
      a Map<V, Integer> mapping each vertex to its SCC id; vertices with the same id are in the same SCC.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if graph is undirected.
